decision.title: Vane is one service with modules and two SDKs (packet book-22)

body.p: , after and . The owner found Vane as a set of services nonsensical: "make it a monolithic service that's fully featured, and we want to offer client libraries/SDKs for frontend and backend, so it's a believable example." The projects, counts, planted flaws and diff shapes of stay; docs/tasks/book.md section 9 has the change table and the packets.

item.p: One service, vane (TypeScript on Node.js), whose parts are modules (api, flags, registry, cache, rollout, audit, db), backed by PostgreSQL and Redis; an evaluation API for the SDKs, an admin API for the console, both as the remote functions of the codegen project (GET /api/getFlags, POST /api/killFlag, ...), and an update stream (the draft's ABNF lines, now rollout-update, kill-update, status-request). Two SDKs: @vane/browser (evaluateFlags for one user) and @vane/node (getFlags, local evaluation, a cache kept current from the stream).

The change keeps its shape in modules: listFlags's N+1 runs against PostgreSQL (report "1 -> 1 + n"), killFlag drops the Redis read and calls the audit module. The new trace participant is the owners' webhook (hooks.example.com), not a service: a monolith has no new service to add, and an audit write alone would only change a count. The trace diff loses its "none ->" version line (nothing new has a resource); that is accepted, and the traces packet teaches the case another way.

The diagram draws modules as boxes labelled vane/MODULE, not a group box: the vocabulary and layout code stay, so draw.xq still writes diagram.svg byte for byte, and no other chapter's diagram changes. Rejected: a group element (new layout machinery for one picture).

Codegen joins the story: it generates the SDK clients (one module per name in api.xml's new clients attribute), the console's client and the service's request validation from vane-api.xsd; the library example goes. The spec keeps its anchors and counts; only wording that described separate services, the ABNF rule names, the Percentage term (rollout by a hash) and req-10 (the SDK's cache) changed.
Packets book-23 to book-29 carry the chapters over (rules of book-15 to book-21: regenerate every output, read it, prose matches, the search words find nothing); book-29 integrates.
